usage: Two servings of pork belly, please
Order at a Korean BBQ place; counted with 인분.
Pork belly with a shot of soju
Classic combo; 에 links the food and drink.
We grill and eat pork belly
굽다 → 구워; you grill it yourself at the table.
Pork belly is the most popular
The default meat most people order first.
examples: 오늘 회식인데 삼겹살 먹으러 가요.
We have a work dinner today, so we're going for pork belly.
삼겹살 is the go-to for casual group dinners.
삼겹살 다 익었어요?
Is the pork belly fully cooked?
익다 = to be cooked; ask before eating off the grill.
삼겹살은 쌈에 싸 먹는 게 맛있어요.
Pork belly tastes great wrapped in lettuce.
쌈 = lettuce wrap; 싸 먹다 = to wrap and eat.
nuance: 삼겹살 literally means 'three-layered flesh,' referring to the streaks of fat and meat. It's the single most iconic Korean BBQ meat and a default social meal, so knowing how to order it by 인분 is genuinely essential for daily life here.
mistakes: Saying 삼겹살 한 개 instead of 삼겹살 1인분 — meat is ordered by serving (인분), not by piece.
Confusing 삼겹살 with 목살 (pork shoulder/neck); they're different cuts on the menu.

usage: 갈비 alone is ambiguous; menus specify 돼지/소.
Counted with 인분 like other BBQ meats.
갈비탕 is a popular beef-rib soup, not grilled.
examples: 여기 양념갈비가 유명해요.
The marinated ribs here are famous.
양념갈비 is the sweet marinated style many foreigners love.
갈비는 좀 비싸지만 가끔 먹을 만해요.
Ribs are a bit pricey, but worth it once in a while.
Beef 갈비 especially is a splurge meat.
점심에 갈비탕 먹으러 갈래요?
Want to go for rib soup at lunch?
갈비탕 is a common, comforting lunch option.
nuance: 갈비 covers the rib cut and a whole family of dishes — grilled 갈비, marinated 양념갈비, and the soup 갈비탕. Because it can be beef or pork, locals always say 소갈비 or 돼지갈비 to be clear, and beef ribs read as a more special, costly meal.
mistakes: Assuming 갈비 always means beef — at many BBQ spots it defaults to pork (돼지갈비).
Mixing up 갈비 (ribs) with 갈비탕 (rib soup); one is grilled, one is a soup dish.

usage: A leaner, premium beef cut at 소고기 restaurants.
부드럽다 = tender/soft, a key selling point.
Two common beef cuts often listed side by side.
Give me the ribeye (flower sirloin), please
꽃등심 = marbled ribeye, a prized upgrade.
examples: 소고깃집에서는 등심이 기본이에요.
At a beef restaurant, sirloin is the standard order.
등심 is the default beef cut for grilling.
꽃등심은 마블링이 좋아서 더 비싸요.
Ribeye has good marbling, so it's pricier.
마블링 (marbling) drives the price of beef cuts.
등심은 너무 익히면 질겨져요.
If you overcook sirloin, it gets tough.
질기다 = tough; lean cuts dry out when overcooked.
nuance: 등심 is the go-to grilling cut at beef-focused restaurants, prized for being relatively lean yet tender. You'll constantly see it next to 안심 and the upgraded 꽃등심 (ribeye) on menus, so recognizing the cut names helps you order beef confidently.
mistakes: Confusing 등심 (sirloin) with 안심 (tenderloin) — 안심 is leaner and more tender.
Ordering 등심 expecting cheap pork; it's almost always a higher-priced beef cut.

usage: The leanest, most tender cut, popular for steak.
Compared to 등심, 안심 is softer.
Ordered by 인분 at beef restaurants.
안심 exists for pork too, often used in cutlets.
examples: 안심은 기름기가 적어서 담백해요.
Tenderloin is low in fat, so it's mild and clean-tasting.
담백하다 describes the lean, non-greasy flavor.
스테이크는 안심으로 주문했어요.
I ordered the steak with tenderloin.
안심 is the classic choice for a tender steak.
안심이라서 좀 더 비쌌어요.
Because it was tenderloin, it was a bit more expensive.
안심 is a premium, leaner cut.
nuance: 안심 is the tenderloin — the leanest and most tender cut, which is why it's the default for steaks. Note it's a homonym of the verb 안심하다 (to feel relieved), so context (a meat menu vs. a conversation) tells you which meaning is intended.
mistakes: Mixing up 안심 (tenderloin) with the verb 안심하다 (to be relieved) — same spelling, totally different meaning.
Assuming 안심 is fattier than 등심; it's actually the leaner of the two.

usage: Give me one chicken drumstick, please
Counted with 개 or 하나 since it's a piece.
살 = the meat; 닭다리살 is boneless leg meat.
Many prefer leg meat over breast (가슴살).
Leg is juicier; breast is leaner.
examples: 치킨 시키면 저는 닭다리부터 먹어요.
When we order fried chicken, I go for the drumstick first.
닭다리 is the favorite piece for many people.
닭다리살로 된 도시락 사 왔어요.
I bought a lunchbox made with chicken leg meat.
닭다리살 (boneless) is common in 도시락 and rice bowls.
애들은 보통 닭다리를 더 좋아해요.
Kids usually like the drumsticks more.
닭다리 is the kid-friendly, easy-to-hold piece.
nuance: 닭다리 is the drumstick/leg, widely seen as the juiciest part of the chicken and often the most fought-over piece when sharing 치킨. The boneless version 닭다리살 shows up in lunchboxes and rice bowls, contrasted with the leaner 닭가슴살 favored by dieters.
mistakes: Counting 닭다리 with 인분 — it's a piece, so use 개 or 하나.
Confusing 닭다리 (leg) with 닭가슴살 (breast); they differ a lot in texture and fat.

usage: Crucial phrase when ordering; 알레르기 = allergy.
튀김 = deep-fried; a very common dish.
빼다 = to remove; useful for allergies or dislikes.
Does it have shrimp in it?
들어가다 here = to be included as an ingredient.
examples: 저 새우 알레르기 있어서 새우는 빼 주세요.
I have a shrimp allergy, so please leave out the shrimp.
Combine allergy + 빼 주세요 to order safely.
이 볶음밥에 새우 들어가요?
Does this fried rice have shrimp in it?
들어가다 asks whether an ingredient is included.
새우튀김이 바삭바삭하고 맛있어요.
The fried shrimp is crispy and delicious.
바삭바삭 describes the crunchy fried texture.
nuance: 새우 (shrimp/prawn) is everywhere in Korean cooking — fried, in fried rice, in stews — so being able to ask 새우 들어가요? and say 새우 빼 주세요 matters a lot for anyone with a shellfish allergy. The plump fried 새우튀김 is a particular favorite.
mistakes: Saying 새우 없어요 to mean 'I can't eat shrimp' — use 새우 빼 주세요 or 새우 알레르기 있어요 instead.
Confusing 새우 (shrimp) with 게 (crab) or 가재 (crayfish); they're separate shellfish.

usage: 볶음 = stir-fry; a popular spicy dish with rice.
질기다 = tough; squid can be rubbery if overcooked.
마르다 → 마른; a classic beer snack (안주).
Counted with 마리 like other animals/seafood.
examples: 오징어볶음은 밥이랑 먹으면 진짜 맛있어요.
Spicy stir-fried squid is really good with rice.
오징어볶음 is a staple spicy rice-pairing dish.
맥주에는 마른 오징어가 최고죠.
Dried squid is the best with beer.
마른 오징어 is a beloved drinking snack.
오징어를 너무 오래 익히면 질겨져요.
If you cook squid too long, it gets rubbery.
질겨지다 = to become tough; cook squid briefly.
nuance: 오징어 (squid) appears as the spicy stir-fry 오징어볶음, as grilled or dried snacks, and on countless seafood menus. Locals know it turns rubbery when overcooked, and dried 마른 오징어 is a quintessential 안주 (drinking snack), so the word comes up in both restaurants and convenience stores.
mistakes: Counting 오징어 with 개 — use 마리 for whole squid (한 마리, 두 마리).
Confusing 오징어 (squid) with 문어 (octopus) or 낙지 (small octopus); they're different on menus.

usage: 구이 = grilled dish; a popular seaside meal.
탕 = soup; light, savory broth from clams.
Unopened clams while cooking shouldn't be eaten.
조개 deepens the broth of 칼국수.
examples: 바닷가에서 조개구이 먹었어요.
We had grilled clams at the seaside.
조개구이 is a classic coastal restaurant order.
이 칼국수는 조개를 많이 넣어서 국물이 시원해요.
This noodle soup has lots of clams, so the broth is refreshing.
시원하다 here describes a clean, savory broth.
조개에서 모래가 나올 수 있으니까 잘 씻어요.
Clams can have sand, so wash them well.
해감 (purging sand) matters before cooking clams.
nuance: 조개 is the general word for clams/shellfish and headlines dishes like 조개구이 (grilled clams) and 조개탕. The broth from clams is described as 시원하다 — a clean, savory 'refreshing' taste rather than cold — which is a very Korean way to praise soup.
mistakes: Translating 국물이 시원해요 as 'the broth is cold' — here 시원하다 means clean and savory.
Using 조개 for a specific clam when the menu wants 바지락 (manila clam) or 홍합 (mussel).

usage: 구이 = grilled; a staple home-style fish dish.
조림 = braised in seasoned sauce, often spicy.
비리다 = fishy-smelling; common with oily fish.
손 = a counter for two fish sold together.
examples: 백반집에서 고등어구이가 자주 나와요.
Grilled mackerel often comes with set-menu meals.
백반 (home-style set meal) frequently includes 고등어구이.
고등어조림은 무랑 같이 조리면 맛있어요.
Braised mackerel is good simmered with radish.
무 (radish) is a classic 조림 pairing.
고등어는 구울 때 냄새가 좀 나요.
Mackerel gives off a bit of a smell when grilled.
Oily fish like 고등어 are aromatic while cooking.
nuance: 고등어 (mackerel) is an everyday, affordable fish that anchors home-style meals as 고등어구이 or 고등어조림. Because it's an oily fish, locals talk about it being 비리다 (fishy) if not fresh, and it's often sold by the 손 (a pair), which is a useful counter to recognize at the market.
mistakes: Calling 고등어 a 조개 or generic 생선 when a recipe specifically needs mackerel.
Saying 고등어 냄새 나빠요 — use 비리다 for the specific fishy smell of seafood.

usage: 초밥 = sushi; 연어 is a top sushi choice in Korea.
덮밥 = rice bowl topped with ingredients.
회 = sliced raw fish; very popular as 연어회.
신선하다 = fresh; key for raw salmon dishes.
examples: 저는 회 중에서 연어를 제일 좋아해요.
Among sashimi, I like salmon the most.
연어 is one of the most popular 회 options.
연어 덮밥 하나랑 미소국 주세요.
One salmon rice bowl and miso soup, please.
연어 덮밥 is a common, easy lunch order.
연어는 구워 먹어도 맛있어요.
Salmon is also delicious grilled.
연어 works raw or cooked (연어구이).
nuance: 연어 (salmon) has become hugely popular in Korea, especially raw as 연어회 or 연어 초밥 and in 연어 덮밥 rice bowls. Unlike many native fish, it's a trendy, mild option newcomers often gravitate to, so it's worth knowing alongside the more traditional 회 fish.
mistakes: Confusing 연어 (salmon) with 송어 (trout); they look similar but are different fish.
Expecting all 회 restaurants to feature 연어 — traditional 횟집 may focus on white fish like 광어.

usage: One serving of grilled intestines, please
곱창 (small intestine), 대창/막창 are other cuts.
Fried rice made after grilling intestines
볶음밥 made in the leftover pan is a must.
examples: 오늘 곱창에 소주 한잔 어때요?
How about grilled intestines and soju tonight?
곱창 is a classic 술안주 (drinking food).
곱창은 호불호가 좀 갈려요.
People are divided on grilled intestines.
호불호가 갈리다 = opinions are split (love it or hate it).
곱창 먹고 마지막에 볶음밥 꼭 먹어요.
After the intestines, we always get fried rice at the end.
Pan-fried 볶음밥 is the traditional finish.
nuance: 곱창 is grilled beef or pork small intestine, a popular but polarizing 술안주 enjoyed late at night with soju. The whole experience usually ends with 볶음밥 fried in the leftover pan, and locals will warn you that 곱창 is a 호불호 food — you either love it or you don't.
mistakes: Lumping 곱창, 대창, and 막창 together — they're distinct cuts of offal with different textures.
Assuming 곱창 is always beef; pork 곱창 (돼지곱창) is common and cheaper.

usage: 회 = raw sliced fish, eaten at a 횟집.
모둠 = assorted; a mix of several fish.
Counted with 접시 (plate) for a serving.
Useful if you don't eat raw seafood.
examples: 바닷가 왔으니까 회 먹어야죠.
Since we're at the coast, we should eat sashimi.
회 is the signature thing to eat near the sea.
모둠회 시키면 여러 종류 나와요.
If you order the assorted platter, you get several kinds.
모둠회 is great when you can't decide.
저는 익힌 게 좋아서 회는 잘 안 먹어요.
I prefer cooked food, so I don't really eat raw fish.
Polite way to say you avoid 회.
nuance: 회 means sliced raw fish (sashimi-style) and is a centerpiece of Korean coastal dining at a 횟집, usually shared as a 모둠회 platter with side dishes. It's deeply tied to seaside trips and drinking, so knowing how to say 회 먹으러 가요 or 회 못 먹어요 covers a very common social situation.
mistakes: Confusing 회 (raw fish) with 초밥 (sushi with rice) — 회 is just the sliced fish.
Pronouncing/writing it as 회사 or other 회 homonyms; context (a 횟집) clarifies the food meaning.
